summary: Earth Echo is first of all a voice tour, with a web tool as its second part. On a phone, it uses GPS to pull NASA POWER data for where you stand and reads the results aloud, one item at a time: temperature, rainfall, humidity and sunshine. On a computer, a world map shows long-term trends for capital cities, built from NASA data. We call something a trend only when it passes a Mann-Kendall test, and every number shows its dataset and years. Climate data is usually hard for ordinary people to read. Earth Echo turns it into a short, plain spoken answer about the place where you stand, so anyone can check what their own place has been telling them.
details: Earth Echo is a voice tour that reads out the local climate data where you stand. It uses GPS and live NASA data, and skips any item with no real data for your location. It turns hard climate data into a plain spoken answer. Being location first and voice first, it lets you hear your own place's story instead of reading a chart. We built it with HTML, JavaScript and Python, use the phone's built-in text-to-speech, and host it on GitHub Pages. Honesty guided every choice: every number shows its data source and years.
